appraisal_events.evidence: Elle prend la main de sa fille en gardant l’autre devant sa bouche « pour donner cette cause apparente à la légère difficulté qu’elle avait encore à prononcer certains mots », et plaisante : « voilà comme tu plains ta mère ! tu as l’air de croire que ce n’est pas désagréable une indigestion ! » ; la mère répond « Maman, tu seras bientôt guérie, c’est ta fille qui s’y engage » et dépose son baiser « humblement, pieusement sur le front adoré ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator stages a fully reciprocated moment of tenderness in which the grandmother conceals her symptoms to spare her daughter and is received as an object of veneration (le front adoré); the gesture is presented with unqualified reverence, so the grandmother is locally elevated even as she is dying.

appraisal_events.evidence: « elle ne se rendait pas compte qu’elle en était elle-même la cause, de sorte que chaque jour elle accusa injustement Françoise de mal “retaper” son lit »
appraisal_events.explanation: The grandmother repeatedly blames Françoise for a discomfort she herself causes; the narrator flatly labels the accusation unjust and supplies its real cause, so the blame is reported and simultaneously invalidated rather than endorsed.

status_effects.explanation: She is locally raised to the position of the adored, self-effacing figure: she hides her difficulty speaking to protect her daughter and receives a pious, worshipful kiss.

The daughter attains a realized, mutually received intimacy with her mother — the first passionate meeting of their eyes and the kiss into which she pours her whole will — though the narrator's gloss on her vow as a false oath keeps the gain short of a full elevation.

Within the household she is accused daily of doing her work badly, a real if unfounded lowering of her standing in the sickroom; the narrator's explicit « injustement » prevents this from becoming a drop in general appraisal.

ambiguities: The surface form « Maman » in the mother's speech addresses the grandmother, not the narrator's mother, even though the reference sheet lists « maman » among the mother's aliases; likewise « ma fille » and « ta fille » denote the mother, and « ta mère » the grandmother. Misresolving these would invert the source and target of E1.

It is genuinely underdetermined whether E2 should move Françoise at all: the narrator both records the accusation as habitual and daily and immediately annuls it as unjust (the prior window even credits her « soins parfaits »), so the reading taken here — a small loss of household standing with no loss of appraisal — is the stronger but not the only defensible one; the alternative is to read the accusation as diminishing only the grandmother's failing self-perception.
